products.name: Ashwagandha KSM-66 Gummies

products.name: Ashwagandha Extract

products.name: Shilajit 500mg

products.name: Shilajit Pure

products.name: Himalayan Shilajit Resin
products.summary: Purified shilajit resin with a disclosed fulvic acid percentage. Better-specified than most Indian shilajit products.

products.name: Safed Musli
products.summary: Chlorophytum borivilianum at 400mg. Male health supplement with limited clinical evidence. No standardisation to active saponins.

products.name: Maca Root 1000mg

products.name: StressCare Ashwagandha

products.name: Ashwagandha Tablets

products.name: Ashwagandha 450mg
products.summary: Generic extract at 450mg. No extract specification (KSM-66 or Sensoril not claimed). Import pricing adds to the opacity.

products.name: Ashwagandha 1000mg
products.summary: Generic root powder. 1000mg is a meaningless dose number without extract specification. Withanolide content unknown.

products.name: HK Vitals Ashwagandha
products.summary: Generic ashwagandha at 500mg with no extract specification. No COA, no withanolide standard. Priced below the KSM-66 floor with reason.

products.name: Ashwagandha Capsule
products.summary: Ayurvedic brand with generic root powder. 500mg per capsule with no withanolide specification. Ayurvedic positioning doesn't compensate.

products.name: Ashwagandha Churna
products.summary: Raw ashwagandha powder — no extract, no standardisation. Traditional format without the quality controls needed for consistent supplementation.

products.name: Ashwagandha 500mg
products.summary: Generic ashwagandha — no extract specification claimed. Priced accordingly. The correct purchase only if budget is the primary constraint.

products.name: Ashwagandha 500mg
products.summary: Generic root extract. No extract specification, no NABL COA. Pharmacy shelf positioning without pharmacy supply chain quality.

products.name: Testosterone Booster
products.summary: D-Aspartic Acid, fenugreek, and ashwagandha at disclosed doses. DAA evidence is weak; fenugreek has mild testosterone data. Mixed formulation.

products.name: Testosterone Booster
products.summary: D-Aspartic Acid with generic ashwagandha and zinc. DAA evidence for testosterone in clinical populations is weak at best. Marketing-led formulation.

products.name: HK Vitals Stress Buster
products.summary: Ashwagandha with L-theanine at undisclosed doses. Combination is logical but doses are opaque — making any evidence attribution impossible.

products.name: Ashwagandha Effervescent
products.summary: Generic ashwagandha in effervescent format at 300mg. No extract specification. Format is novel; base formulation is under-specified.

products.name: Ashwagandha Gold Capsule
products.summary: Ashwagandha with milk. No extract specification. 'Gold' naming implies premium positioning the ingredient cannot support without withanolide data.

products.name: Ashwagandha Shatavar Kapi Kacchu
products.summary: Testosterone-support Ayurvedic formula. Mucuna pruriens has L-DOPA content with real male health data. Doses are undisclosed.

products.name: Men's Ultivite Multivitamin
products.summary: Australian multivitamin with ginseng addition at 200mg. Ginseng dose at this level adds minimal benefit. Multi quality is acceptable.

products.name: Boron
products.summary: Boron glycinate at 3mg — within the range used in testosterone and estrogen metabolism trials. Niche micromineral supplement with growing evidence.

products.name: Ashwagandhadi Lehyam
products.summary: Traditional ashwagandha formulation in a ghee-honey base. Authentic preparation format. No withanolide specification — traditional dose.

products.name: Ashwagandha Capsule
products.summary: Generic root extract at 500mg. No withanolide specification. Dabur's supply chain quality is consistent — the formulation is not.

products.name: Brahmi Vati
products.summary: Brahmi at unstandardised dose in traditional tablet form. Bacosides specification is absent. Brahmi evidence requires standardised extract.

products.name: Mentat Brain Tonic
products.summary: Brahmi-led nootropic formula. Brahmi evidence requires standardised extract — tablet form makes dose and standardisation opaque.

products.name: Shatavari 1000mg
products.summary: Shatavari root powder at 1000mg. No saponin standardisation disclosed. Used for women's health — clinical evidence is limited and unstandardised.

products.name: Ginseng Extract
products.summary: Panax ginseng at an undisclosed mg with unstated ginsenoside percentage. Generic ginseng at a pharmacy price without extract specification.

products.name: Ashwagandha Powder
products.summary: Unsupplemented root powder. No extract specification, no withanolide standard. Traditional whole-food use case — not a supplement.

products.name: Get Slim Juice
products.summary: A herbal blend at homeopathic doses with weight-loss claims that no individual ingredient supports at the included amount.

products.name: Liv.52 DS
products.summary: The only AYUSH hepatoprotective with a completed RCT in alcoholic liver disease. Not a supplement — a drug with evidence. Context matters.

products.name: Cystone
products.summary: Kidney stone prevention multi-herb formula. Has a small but genuine RCT base for ureteral stone passage and kidney stone recurrence reduction.

products.name: Septilin
products.summary: Immunostimulant multi-herb preparation. The most RCT-studied herbal immune product from Himalaya. Evidence quality is modest but it exists.

products.name: Rumalaya Forte
products.summary: Joint health multi-herb. Boswellia, guggul, and shallaki — all have anti-inflammatory evidence. Extract quality across the blend varies.

products.name: Evecare
products.summary: Women's menstrual health multi-herb formula. Himalaya-funded clinical study in secondary amenorrhoea. Evidence is brand-funded but exists.

products.name: Confido
products.summary: Male sexual wellness formula. Small Himalaya-funded RCT in premature ejaculation. Evidence is limited in scope but it is real evidence.

products.name: Chyawanprash
products.summary: Amla-primary polyherbal preparation with real antioxidant evidence for the Amla component. The rest of the formula is traditional and unquantified.

products.name: Geriforte
products.summary: Anti-stress and anti-ageing multi-herb formula. Long product history. Small number of industry-sponsored RCTs on subjective wellbeing outcomes.

products.name: Abana Heart Care
products.summary: Cardiovascular herbal formula. Some evidence for arjuna (Terminalia arjuna) in heart failure management. Other components are supportive.

products.name: Diabecon
products.summary: Anti-diabetic herbal formula with gymnema and shilajit. Some small Himalaya-sponsored studies in borderline hyperglycaemia. Not a diabetes treatment.

products.name: Tentex Forte
products.summary: Male sexual function multi-herb. Small number of Himalaya-sponsored RCTs on erectile function. Evidence is narrow but brand-funded studies do exist.

products.name: Pure Herbs Shankhpushpi
products.summary: Convolvulus pluricaulis for cognitive support. Traditional Ayurvedic use — limited modern RCT evidence. Extract specification is absent.

products.name: Vrikshamla Garcinia
products.summary: Garcinia cambogia HCA extract for weight management. Multiple meta-analyses show small, inconsistent effects. Not a meaningful weight loss product.

products.name: Pilex
products.summary: Piles management multi-herb formula. Clinical use case is real. Small Himalaya-funded RCT for haemorrhoid symptom reduction exists.

products.name: Triphala Churna
products.summary: Classic Ayurvedic bowel regulator with amla, haritaki, and bibhitaki. Modest clinical evidence for constipation relief. Standard preparation.

products.name: Giloy Juice
products.summary: Tinospora cordifolia juice. Immunomodulatory evidence is in vitro dominant. Post-COVID marketing has significantly overstated the clinical evidence.

products.name: Amla Juice
products.summary: Amla at therapeutic doses has strong antioxidant and cholesterol evidence. Juice format has variable bioavailability vs. standardised extract.

products.name: Triphala Tablet
products.summary: Triphala at an unstandardised dose in tablet form. More convenient than churna. Same evidence ceiling as the powder — bowel regulation only.

products.name: Divya Medohar Vati
products.summary: Proprietary Ayurvedic weight loss formula. No clinical trial evidence. Formulation is opaque. Sold with claims that no ingredient supports.

products.name: Swasari Vati
products.summary: Respiratory herbal formulation. Traditional use for cough and bronchitis. Limited modern RCT evidence. AYUSH licensed product.

products.name: Arjuna Bark
products.summary: Terminalia arjuna extract — genuine evidence for cardiovascular function. Dose and standardisation are opaque in Patanjali's formulation.

products.name: Shatavar Churna
products.summary: Asparagus racemosus powder — the traditional women's health herb. No saponin standardisation. Traditional use with limited modern RCT evidence.

products.name: Coronil
products.summary: Post-COVID herbal. AYUSH-licensed claims. The single Patanjali study was retracted. Regulatory approval is not equivalent to clinical evidence.

products.name: Giloy Neem Juice
products.summary: Tinospora + Azadirachta combination. Both have immunomodulatory traditional use. RCT evidence for the combination is non-existent.

products.name: Stressnil
products.summary: Ashwagandha + Brahmi combination at unstandardised doses. Concept is sound; execution without extract specification limits clinical confidence.

products.name: Ratnaprash
products.summary: Gold-enriched chyawanprash variant. Gold is at pharmacologically irrelevant concentrations. Premium pricing for the perception of gold.

products.name: Tulsi Drops
products.summary: Holy basil (Ocimum sanctum) extract drops. Adaptogenic and mild immunomodulatory evidence. Dose per serving is difficult to quantify.

products.name: Shilajit Gold
products.summary: Shilajit with gold and ashwagandha. 'Gold' is at pharmacologically irrelevant doses. Shilajit component specification is undisclosed.

products.name: Trifgol
products.summary: Psyllium husk based dietary fibre supplement. Genuine evidence for LDL reduction and bowel regularity. Functional fibre — not herbal extracts.

products.name: Aloe Vera Juice
products.summary: Aloe vera juice with GI benefit evidence for constipation. Claims around immunity and detox are unsupported. The GI use case is legitimate.

products.name: Apple Cider Vinegar
products.summary: ACV at 30ml/day. Clinical evidence for metabolic benefit is weak across all claimed domains — glycaemic, weight, digestive.

products.name: Noni Juice
products.summary: Noni fruit juice with broad health claims. The clinical evidence for noni (Morinda citrifolia) is preliminary and largely in vitro.

products.name: Karela Jamun Juice
products.summary: Similar to the Himalaya product — karela's blood glucose evidence is real but variable without dose standardisation.

products.name: Tulsi Giloy Amla Juice
products.summary: Triple-herb juice blend. The combination has broad wellness claims without any individual herb at a clinical dose. Polypharmacy for marketing.

products.name: Vitality Juice
products.summary: Multi-herbal energy juice. Claims range across immunity, energy, and stamina without any single ingredient at a clinical dose.

products.name: Diabetes Care Juice
products.summary: Karela-dominant blood sugar juice with broad diabetes management claims. Karela evidence is modest — the product claim exceeds what evidence supports.

products.name: Musli Power
products.summary: Safed musli (Chlorophytum borivilianum) supplement for male health. Some small RCT evidence. Saponin standardisation is not disclosed.

products.name: Brahmi Juice
products.summary: Brahmi juice — raw plant juice at unknown bacosides concentration. Without standardisation the cognitive evidence cannot be applied.

products.name: Ashwagandha Gummies
products.summary: Generic ashwagandha at undisclosed extract specification in a sugar-containing gummy. Format prioritised over formulation quality.

products.name: Moringa Powder
products.summary: Moringa oleifera leaf powder at 3g per serving. Genuinely nutrient-dense food supplement. Claims beyond nutrition are not well-evidenced.

products.name: Happy Soul
products.summary: 'Mood support' herbal blend. No individual ingredient is at a dose with clinical evidence for mood modulation. Label claims significantly exceed evidence.

products.name: Triphala
products.summary: Triphala at 1000mg per serving. No standardisation to individual actives. Consistent with the general category quality ceiling.

products.name: Fenugreek Seed Extract
products.summary: Fenugreek at 500mg standardised to 50% saponins. Real evidence for blood sugar and modest testosterone effect. Correct standardisation cited.

products.name: Green Coffee Bean
products.summary: Chlorogenic acid-standardised green coffee extract. Modest weight management evidence in short-duration RCTs. Effect size is clinically small.

products.name: Coleus Forskohlii
products.summary: Forskolin at 250mg standardised to 20% coleusin. Modest cAMP-mediated fat mobilisation evidence. Effect size in human RCTs is small.

products.name: Neem Capsule
products.summary: Azadirachta indica extract at 500mg. Antibacterial and anti-inflammatory evidence exists. Dose and standardisation are modest.

products.name: Gokshura Extract
products.summary: Tribulus terrestris extract with protodioscin specification. Modest but real evidence for urinary tract function. Testosterone claims are weak.

products.name: Terminalia Arjuna
products.summary: Arjuna bark extract at 500mg with no tannin standardisation. Cardiovascular evidence for arjuna is the strongest in any Indian herbal product.

products.name: Black Cumin Seed Oil
products.summary: Nigella sativa oil at 500mg. TQ (thymoquinone) content is not disclosed. Moderate evidence for anti-inflammatory and immune effects.

products.name: Immunity Booster
products.summary: Multi-herb immunity blend with giloy, neem, tulsi at undisclosed and likely sub-clinical doses. Broad immunity claim with no specific evidence.

products.name: Liver Detox
products.summary: Multi-herb liver formula with 'detox' claims. 'Detox' as a supplement category has no credible clinical definition or endpoint.

products.name: Spirulina Powder
products.summary: Spirulina at 5g per serving — the dose used in cholesterol and blood pressure trials. The evidence is modest but the dose is correct.

products.name: Curcumin BCM-95 (Herbal)

products.name: Alpha Lipoic Acid (Herbal)
products.summary: 600mg ALA per capsule. NABL COA. One of the few domestic ALA options with documentation. Antioxidant and neuroprotective RCT evidence.

products.name: Ashwagandharishta
products.summary: Traditional liquid ashwagandha formulation with alcohol as carrier. Difficult to quantify active dose. Ayurvedic format, not supplement.

products.name: Pancharishta
products.summary: Multi-herb digestive tonic in arishtam form. Long traditional use. Dose of each herb is uncontrolled — efficacy is variable.

products.name: Makardhwaj Vati
products.summary: Traditional mercury-gold preparation. Heavy metal content makes this a regulatory grey area — not suitable for self-supplementation.

products.name: Karela Jamun Juice
products.summary: Bitter gourd and Indian blackberry juice. Modest blood sugar evidence for karela. Dose standardisation is absent — effect size is variable.

products.name: Mentat DS Syrup
products.summary: Brahmi-led nootropic syrup from Himalaya. Brahmi evidence requires standardised extract — syrup form makes dose and standardisation opaque.

products.name: Moringa Capsule
products.summary: Moringa oleifera leaf extract in capsule. More standardised delivery than powder. Nutrient-dense — food supplement category, not drug.

products.name: Bonnisan
products.summary: Paediatric digestive formulation. Not a supplement — a child-specific Ayurvedic GI product. Frequently confused with supplement products.

products.name: Nutri Power Biscuits
products.summary: Fortified biscuits with herbal additions. Not a supplement. Nutrient content is primarily from the biscuit base — not the herb.

products.name: Mulethi Powder
products.summary: Licorice root powder for sore throat and gut. Real GI and anti-inflammatory evidence for glycyrrhizin. Dose control is the issue.

products.name: Amla Reetha Shikakai Juice
products.summary: Topical hair care ingredients in juice form. No clinical evidence for internal hair health benefit from Reetha or Shikakai.

products.name: Ashwagandha Shatavar
products.summary: Combined formula with no extract specification for either herb. Raw powder combination at prices that reflect the input cost — not a supplement.

products.name: Honitus Syrup
products.summary: Cough and cold relief with tulsi, ginger, and mulethi. Traditional respiratory formula — OTC product marketed alongside supplements.

products.name: Ashwagandha 1000mg (Herbal)
products.summary: Generic ashwagandha root powder. 1000mg is meaningless without extract specification. Popular search term, poor ingredient transparency.

products.name: Fish Oil 1000mg
products.summary: Online-first brand. Standard concentration. No freshness documentation. Adequate as a last resort — not a first choice.

products.name: Moringa Powder
products.summary: Moringa oleifera powder at high doses. Nutrient-dense but not a standardised supplement — closer to a food supplement. Claims exceed evidence.

products.name: HK Vitals Ginseng
products.summary: Generic Panax ginseng with no ginsenoside specification. Budget brand with an adaptogen claim that requires more than the label provides.

products.name: Astaxanthin 8mg
products.summary: Haematococcus pluvialis derived astaxanthin at 8mg — the most commonly used research dose. Antioxidant evidence is moderate. Correctly specified.

products.name: Organic Wheat Grass Juice
products.summary: Wheatgrass powder dissolved in water. Chlorophyll content and 'detox' claims are marketing without human RCT basis.

products.name: Punarnava Mandur
products.summary: Iron-herb combination for anaemia and fluid retention. Traditional use with limited modern trials. Heavy metal content possible in classical preparation.

products.name: Shatavar Avaleha
products.summary: Traditional women's tonic in avaleha form. Asparagus racemosus at undisclosed dose. Format is traditional — not supplement-grade.

products.name: Divya Swarna Maksika Bhasma
products.summary: Gold-copper pyrite bhasma — a heavy metal-containing traditional preparation. Not suitable for unsupervised supplementation.

products.name: Mulethi Licorice
products.summary: Glycyrrhiza glabra extract. GI and anti-inflammatory evidence exists. Glycyrrhizin content should be monitored with long-term use — blood pressure risk.

products.name: Brahmi Bacopa
products.summary: Bacopa monnieri at 500mg with no bacoside specification. Brahmi evidence is real — but without standardisation, dosing is guesswork.

products.name: Caffeine + L-Theanine

products.name: Caffeine 200mg
products.summary: Pure caffeine anhydrous at 200mg per capsule. Batch COA on website. The utility supplement — evidence is overwhelming, documentation is correct.

products.name: Caffeine 200mg
products.summary: 200mg caffeine anhydrous. No COA. Correctly dosed. The evidence for caffeine as an ergogenic aid is settled — this is a safe commodity purchase.

products.name: L-Carnitine Tartrate
products.summary: 2g L-carnitine tartrate per serving. Batch COA on Nutrabay. Evidence for fat oxidation in trained adults is modest and consistent.

products.name: L-Carnitine L-Tartrate
products.summary: 2g per serving, NABL COA, no additives. The value benchmark for documented carnitine in India. Evidence: moderate for trained athletes.

products.name: C4 Original Pre Workout

products.summary: Beta-alanine 1.5g, caffeine 175mg, creatine 3g. Conservative doses — clean label, honest formula. Import pricing is the only objection.

products.name: The Pre-Workout
products.summary: Informed Sport certified. Citrulline 4g, caffeine 200mg. Doses are disclosed. Sale pricing makes it competitive with domestic options.

products.name: Pre Workout Fuego
products.summary: Full-disclosure label with beta-alanine at 3.2g and caffeine at 200mg. One of the few Indian pre-workouts without a proprietary blend.

products.name: Ripped Extreme Pre Workout
products.summary: Proprietary blend with total weight disclosed but individual doses hidden. Caffeine content unspecified — a significant problem for sensitive users.

products.name: PRE + Post Workout
products.summary: Combined pre and post-workout formula. Pre ingredients are at partial doses to make room for the post-workout blend — neither is done fully.

products.name: L-Citrulline Malate
products.summary: 6g citrulline malate per serving. Batch COA on website. The best standalone pump ingredient in the domestic market for the price.

products.name: Beta Alanine

products.name: L-Arginine 3000mg
products.summary: 3g arginine per serving. NABL COA. Arginine has modest vasodilation evidence — citrulline is pharmacokinetically superior but arginine is cheaper.

products.name: Xtend BCAAs
products.summary: 2:1:1 BCAA ratio at 7g per serving with 2.5g leucine. Electrolytes added. Informed Choice certified. The reference BCAA on the Indian market.

products.name: BCAA Pro
products.summary: 7g BCAA at 2:1:1 ratio. Domestic label with disclosed doses. No third-party certification but dose transparency is above the domestic average.

products.name: BCAA 2:1:1
products.summary: NABL COA, 7g per serving, no flavouring or dyes. The value benchmark for documented BCAAs in India. Unflavoured only — that is a feature.

products.name: Instantized BCAA
products.summary: 5g BCAA per serving. Labdoor A rating. Clean label, instant mixing, widely available. Import pricing is higher than domestic NABL options.

products.name: BCAA 8:1:1
products.summary: Higher leucine ratio — 8g leucine per serving. Batch COA. The leucine-heavy ratio is plausible but not better-evidenced than 2:1:1 in RCTs.

products.name: L-Glutamine 5000mg
products.summary: 5g glutamine per serving. NABL COA. Evidence for gut health and recovery is moderate. The domestic benchmark for documented glutamine.

products.name: L-Glutamine Powder
products.summary: 5g pure glutamine. NABL COA. No additives, no flavouring. The reference domestic glutamine for purity-focused buyers.

products.name: EAA + Hydration
products.summary: Full EAA panel with disclosed individual amino acids. Coconut water powder for electrolytes. Informed Sport certified. The premium EAA reference.

products.name: Essential Amino Acids
products.summary: Complete EAA panel with disclosed per-amino-acid doses. Batch COA on Nutrabay website. Best-documented domestic EAA product.

products.name: Amino Blend
products.summary: EAA blend with undisclosed individual amino acid doses. The proprietary blend obscures leucine content — the most important variable.

products.summary: 1500mg glucosamine sulphate, 1200mg chondroitin sulphate — the doses used in the GAIT trial. NABL COA. Domestic reference for joint supplements.

products.name: Glucosamine + MSM
products.summary: 1500mg glucosamine sulphate with 1500mg MSM. USP verified. Both compounds at clinical doses. The import reference for joint health.

products.summary: Boswellia serrata, glucosamine, and chondroitin. Boswellia dose is 300mg without AKBA % disclosure — the key quality gap.

products.name: Glucosamine 1500mg
products.summary: Glucosamine sulphate at the studied dose. No independent COA. Useful for osteoarthritis symptom management — evidence is moderate and consistent.

products.name: Boswellia Serrata 500mg
products.summary: Boswellia extract standardised to 65% boswellic acids with AKBA content disclosed. NABL COA. The domestic benchmark for documented boswellia.

products.name: Collagen + Glucosamine
products.summary: 10g hydrolyzed collagen with 750mg glucosamine. Combined approach for joint matrix support. Industry-funded RCT support for both components.

products.name: Glucosamine Hyaluronic Acid Chondroitin MSM
products.summary: Four-compound joint formula at clinical doses. Hyaluronic acid addition with evidence for knee osteoarthritis. Solgar quality standard throughout.

products.name: Joint Relief
products.summary: Sport brand joint formula. Boswellia at meaningful dose, glucosamine and chondroitin at standard doses. Better ingredient disclosure than most.

products.name: L-Theanine 200mg
products.summary: L-theanine at 200mg — the dose used in sleep quality and anxiety RCTs. NABL COA. The domestic reference for documented theanine.

products.summary: Melatonin 3mg with L-theanine 200mg and ashwagandha. The combination is synergistic in theory. Individual doses are all at meaningful levels.

products.name: Melatonin 5mg

products.name: GABA 500mg
products.summary: 500mg GABA per capsule. Blood-brain barrier crossing of oral GABA is debated — the anxiolytic effect seen in some trials may be peripheral.

products.name: Melatonin 5mg
products.summary: 5mg melatonin softgel. Import brand with consistent quality. Dose is higher than minimum effective — not dangerous but likely more than needed.

products.name: Probiotic 50 Billion
products.summary: 50 billion CFU, 11 strains, strain identity fully disclosed. NABL COA. The highest-CFU domestic probiotic with proper documentation.

products.name: Daily Greens
products.summary: Greens powder with spirulina, chlorella, and wheatgrass. Nutrient claims are modest. No standardisation to active compounds. Habit-building product.

products.name: Phosphatidylserine 100mg
products.summary: PS at 100mg per capsule — the FDA-qualified health claim dose for cognitive decline. NABL COA. Correctly specified niche nootropic.

products.name: Ginkgo Biloba 120mg
products.summary: GBE-761 standardisation at 120mg. USP verified. The import reference for documented ginkgo. Reliable quality at a reasonable import price.

products.name: Bacopa Monnieri 300mg
products.summary: Bacopa at 300mg standardised to 20% bacosides. Correct specification for the cognitive RCT evidence base. Well-priced domestic option.

products.name: Lion's Mane 500mg
products.summary: Hericium erinaceus at 500mg. Beta-glucan content not disclosed. Emerging cognitive evidence is promising but the specification gap reduces confidence.

products.name: MentalFocus Brahmi
products.summary: Brahmi + gotu kola combination. Individual doses and extract specifications are not disclosed. The combination has logic but lacks specification.

products.name: Biotin 5000 mcg

products.name: Biotin 10000 mcg
products.summary: 10mg biotin — the full clinical dose used in hair and nail brittle trials. Third-party partial documentation. Correct dose.

products.name: Skin Melts Biotin + Zinc
products.summary: Biotin 10mg with zinc gluconate in strip format. Both at meaningful doses. Strip format for biotin has some sublingual logic.

products.name: Marine Collagen 5000mg
products.summary: Marine-sourced hydrolyzed collagen peptides at 5g per serving. Type I collagen. Skin hydration and wrinkle RCT evidence exists for this dose.

products.name: Hair Vitamins
products.summary: Multi-nutrient hair formula. Biotin is at clinical dose (5000mcg). Other ingredients are at sub-clinical amounts. Biotin alone is doing the work.

products.name: Ultra Nourish Hair
products.summary: Biotin 5000mcg with saw palmetto and collagen. Saw palmetto dose is sub-clinical. The biotin is the only evidence-based component at a real dose.

products.name: CLA 1000mg
products.summary: Conjugated linoleic acid at 1g per softgel. Pooled RCT evidence shows small fat mass reduction at 3-4g/day — you need 3-4 capsules.

products.name: Fat Burner
products.summary: Proprietary thermogenic blend with L-carnitine and CLA. Neither ingredient is particularly effective for fat loss in RCTs at typical doses.

products.name: Thermogenic

products.name: Women's Multivitamin

products.name: Iron + Folic Acid + B12

products.name: Plant-Based Iron + Vitamin C

products.name: Shatavari 1000mg

products.name: Reload Electrolyte

products.name: Electrolytes Pro

products.name: VM-75 Multivitamin

products.name: Daily Vits Multivitamin

products.name: Men's Multivitamin

products.name: Multivitamin + Minerals
products.summary: Broad-coverage multi with partially active forms. Batch COA on Nutrabay website. Better transparency than most domestic multivitamin brands.

products.name: Plant-Based Multivitamin
products.summary: Vegan multi with whole-food-derived nutrients. Active B forms throughout. Suitable for strict vegetarians who want documented plant-based sourcing.

products.name: Multivitamin Tablet

products.name: Multivitamin + Mineral

products.name: MB Vite Daily Multivitamin
products.summary: Sport-positioned multi with B-complex emphasis. Cyanocobalamin still present. Better than standard budget multi in terms of dose levels.

products.summary: Budget multi with suboptimal forms throughout. Cyanocobalamin, oxide minerals, and beta-carotene. All form selections are inferior.

products.name: HK Vitals Iron Folic Acid B12
products.summary: Standard prenatal mineral combination. Iron as ferrous fumarate (mid-tier), B12 as cyanocobalamin (inferior form). Functionally adequate.

products.name: Vitamin D3 5000 IU
products.summary: D3 at 5000 IU — a therapeutic correction dose. Appropriate for rapid deficiency correction under medical guidance. Not a daily maintenance dose.

products.name: Daily Protein

products.name: Turm-Ric Active Melts
products.summary: Curcumin with piperine and boswellia in strip format. Curcumin specification is not disclosed — without curcuminoid % the dose is opaque.

products.name: Vitamin D3 Vegan Gummies

products.name: Magnesium Taurate

products.name: Selenium 200mcg

products.name: Magnesium Glycinate 400mg

products.name: Chromium Picolinate

products.name: Vitamin K2 MK4 + MK7
products.summary: Combined MK-4 and MK-7 at 100mcg each. MK-7 for sustained daily coverage, MK-4 for tissue-specific targets. NABL COA.

products.name: Triple Glucosamine
products.summary: 1500mg glucosamine with 1200mg chondroitin and 500mg MSM. Import brand. USP-grade ingredients. Conservative but honest formulation.

products.name: Boswellia Curcumin
products.summary: Boswellia with generic turmeric. Boswellia dose and AKBA percentage undisclosed. Curcumin is not standardised extract. Both components under-specified.

products.name: Plant Protein Greens
products.summary: Pea protein with greens blend. Protein content is adequate at 22g. Greens doses are decorative. A decent protein supplement with a marketing layer.

products.name: Menopause Wellness
products.summary: Soy isoflavones, black cohosh, and calcium for menopause symptom management. Black cohosh has limited RCT evidence for hot flashes.

products.name: Daily Multivitamin
products.summary: Domestic mid-tier multi. Some improved mineral forms. No batch COA on the website. Adequate for general use — not for analytical buyers.

products.name: Collagen Builder Vitamin C
products.summary: Vitamin C with amla — marketed as collagen support. Vitamin C is required for collagen synthesis but this is not a collagen supplement.

products.name: Bacopa Brahmi
products.summary: Bacopa monnieri at 500mg without bacoside standardisation. Brahmi evidence is real but requires a standardised extract to be applicable.

products.name: Ashwagandha KSM-66 Melts

products.name: Karela

products.name: Berberine 500mg

products.name: Berberine 500mg

products.name: Berberine 500mg
products.summary: Berberine at 500mg with batch COA on Nutrabay website. Growing evidence base — the most documented metabolic herbal compound after curcumin.

products.name: Quercetin 500mg
products.summary: Quercetin at 500mg. Anti-inflammatory and senolytic evidence is emerging. Most compelling data is in vitro — human RCTs are limited.

products.name: Quercetin 500mg
products.summary: Quercetin at 500mg. NABL COA. The evidence base is emerging — anti-inflammatory and exercise recovery data is modest but real.

products.name: Vitamin K2 D3 Omega3
products.summary: Three-compound combination. Individual doses are below optimal: D3 1000 IU (conservative), K2 45mcg (floor), omega-3 undisclosed EPA+DHA.

products.name: Calcium Magnesium Zinc D3
products.summary: Four-mineral combination in strip format. Calcium as carbonate (less preferred form). Magnesium and zinc are well-chosen. D3 at 1000 IU is conservative.

products.name: Pre + Probiotic
products.summary: Multi-strain probiotic with prebiotic inulin. Batch COA on Nutrabay website. 10B CFU, 6 strains with disclosed identity. Competitive with Purayati.

products.name: Triple Strength Magnesium
products.summary: Magnesium as glycinate, citrate, and malate blend. 300mg elemental. Triple form blend diversifies absorption routes — more marketing than necessity.

products.name: Zinc Magnesium B6
products.summary: ZMA formula — zinc, magnesium, and B6. The ZMA trial evidence for testosterone and sleep is modest and mostly in athletes with deficiency.

products.name: ZMA Zinc Magnesium B6
products.summary: Zinc as monomethionine, magnesium as glycinate, B6 as P5P. All three active forms. NABL COA. The best-formulated domestic ZMA.

products.name: Mushroom Complex
products.summary: Reishi, lion's mane, cordyceps, and chaga blend. Individual doses are not disclosed — making any evidence attribution impossible.

products.name: Cordyceps Sinensis
products.summary: Cordyceps at 500mg with cordycepin content disclosed. Evidence for aerobic performance is modest. Correctly specified for the adaptogen evidence.

products.name: Ashwagandha + Shilajit

products.name: HK Vitals Shilajit
products.summary: Shilajit extract at 500mg with no fulvic acid disclosure. HealthKart house brand — no batch COA. The key specification missing for a premium ingredient.

products.name: Ginger Extract

products.name: Milk Thistle Silymarin

products.name: Silymarin Milk Thistle
products.summary: USP verified silymarin at 150mg, 80% flavonolignans. Milk thistle evidence for liver protection (hepatoprotection) is among the strongest in the herbal category.

products.name: Saw Palmetto

products.name: Valerian Root
products.summary: Valerian at 400mg for sleep. Modest evidence for sleep latency reduction. No valerenic acid standardisation — the active compound specification is absent.

products.name: Ashwagandha + Brahmi
products.summary: KSM-66 at 600mg with Brahmi at 300mg standardised to 20% bacosides. Both at correct doses. Batch COA. The domestic reference for this combination.

products.name: Panax Ginseng 400mg
products.summary: Panax ginseng at 400mg. Ginsenoside specification is not disclosed — the key quality gap for ginseng. Dose is in range for cognitive effects.

products.name: Eleuthero Siberian Ginseng
products.summary: Eleutherococcus senticosus — not Panax ginseng. Different adaptogen with different evidence base. The naming is often confused.

products.name: Magnesium Malate 800mg
products.summary: Magnesium malate at 800mg elemental. Malate form has specific evidence for fibromyalgia fatigue reduction. NABL COA. Niche but correctly specified.

products.name: Potassium 99mg

products.name: Iodine Potassium Iodide

products.name: L-Tyrosine 500mg
products.summary: L-tyrosine at 500mg. NABL COA. Evidence for cognitive performance under stress is RCT-supported. Correct dose for the evidence base.

products.name: Resveratrol 250mg

products.name: Resveratrol 250mg
products.summary: Resveratrol at 250mg. NABL COA. Evidence tier: early-stage human RCT with some cardiovascular benefit. Correctly cautious marketing.

products.name: EGCG Green Tea Extract
products.summary: Decaffeinated green tea extract at 400mg, 90% polyphenols. USP verified. Evidence for antioxidant and modest metabolic effects is reasonable.

products.summary: Green tea extract at 500mg, standardised to 50% EGCG. NABL COA. The domestic benchmark for documented green tea supplementation.

products.summary: Mixed tocotrienols at 100mg — the form with emerging cardiovascular evidence superior to alpha-tocopherol for some outcomes. Correct premium E form.

products.summary: Premium multi with full-spectrum phytonutrients, active B forms, and Solgar's rigorous in-house testing standards. The gold standard broad-spectrum supplement.

products.summary: Women's multi with active B forms, iron as bisglycinate, and cranberry extract. USP verified. The reference women's multi for import buyers.

products.summary: Maca at 500mg with ashwagandha at 300mg. No extract specifications for either. The combination is logical but under-specified.

products.summary: Silymarin at 500mg with 70% flavonolignans. Higher dose but lower standardisation than Carbamide Forte. No COA for Indian market batches.

products.name: Turmeric Curcumin BCM-95
products.summary: BCM-95 extract — a legitimate patented curcumin form with 95% curcuminoids and enhanced bioavailability through ar-turmerone. No batch COA.

products.name: Curcumin Phospholipid Complex
products.summary: Meriva-equivalent phospholipid-bound curcumin at 500mg. Superior bioavailability over standard curcumin extract. NABL COA. Patented form documented.

products.name: Curcumin Phytosome
products.summary: Meriva curcumin phytosome — phospholipid complex with the most extensive bioavailability RCTs for any curcumin form. USP verified. Import reference.

products.name: Curcumin + Piperine
products.summary: Standard curcumin extract with piperine. BioPerine/piperine approach improves bioavailability ~20-fold vs. plain curcumin. Correct but not optimal form.

products.name: Amla Extract 500mg
products.summary: Amla extract standardised to 40% tannins at 500mg. Better specified than juice format. Strong antioxidant and cholesterol evidence at this form.

products.name: Kalonji Black Seed
products.summary: Nigella sativa (black seed) at 500mg as cold-pressed oil. TQ content not disclosed. Anti-inflammatory evidence is moderate with correct form.

products.name: Trikatu
products.summary: Traditional three-pepper combination (black pepper, ginger, long pepper). Used for digestive fire — Ayurvedic use is legitimate. Dose is traditional.

products.name: Spirulina Chlorella
products.summary: Spirulina and chlorella combination. Both at meaningful doses for antioxidant and nutrient density benefits. Evidence is modest but real.

products.name: Wheatgrass Powder
products.summary: Wheatgrass powder at 3g per serving. Nutrient-dense whole food supplement. Claims beyond nutritional support are not well-evidenced.

products.name: Guduchi + Neem
products.summary: Dual immunity herb combination. Both have immunomodulatory traditional use and limited modern evidence. No dose standardisation for either.

products.name: Triphala Churna
products.summary: Traditional Triphala powder. Long traditional use as bowel regulator. Modest evidence for constipation. No standardisation to individual actives.

products.name: Liver Care Plus
products.summary: Multi-herb liver formula marketed as 'liver detox'. The detox claim has no credible clinical definition. Milk thistle is under-dosed.

products.name: Digestive Enzyme Complex
products.summary: Amylase, lipase, protease blend. Digestive enzyme supplementation has real evidence for pancreatic insufficiency. Benefit in healthy adults is modest.

products.name: Digestive Enzyme 10X
products.summary: 10-enzyme complex with protease, amylase, lipase, and lactase. NABL COA. Useful for lactose intolerance and IBS. Better-specified than most domestic options.

products.name: Cinnamon Extract
products.summary: Ceylon cinnamon extract at 500mg. Blood glucose modulation evidence is modest. Ceylon vs. Cassia distinction is important — the safer form is used here.

products.name: Gymnema Sylvestre
products.summary: Gymnema at 400mg standardised to 25% gymnemic acids. Appetite reduction and blood glucose evidence is modest. Correct standardisation cited.

products.name: Dandelion Root
products.summary: Taraxacum officinale root at 500mg. Diuretic and liver support use in traditional medicine. Clinical evidence is limited and mostly in vitro.

products.name: Senna Leaf
products.summary: Senna as a laxative — the active glycosides are pharmacologically real. This is an OTC laxative, not a supplement. Overuse causes dependency.

products.name: Psyllium Husk Powder
products.summary: Psyllium at 5g per serving. Strong evidence for LDL reduction, blood glucose, and bowel regularity. The most evidence-backed fibre supplement.

products.name: Psyllium Husk 1000mg
products.summary: Psyllium at 1g per capsule. NABL COA. Strong clinical evidence for LDL reduction and GI health. The reference domestic psyllium supplement.

products.name: Basic B Complex
products.summary: Active B vitamin forms throughout — methylcobalamin, methylfolate, P5P. NSF Certified for Sport. The import reference for active-form B complex.

products.name: Vitamin D/K2
products.summary: D3 at 1000 IU with MK-4 form K2 at 200mcg. NSF Certified. Thorne's supply chain documentation is among the most rigorous available in India.

products.name: Magnesium Glycinate
products.summary: Pharmaceutical-grade glycinate chelate with hypoallergenic formulation. USP verified. The reference magnesium for clinically sensitive users in India.

products.name: Vitamin D3 2000 IU
products.summary: Hypoallergenic D3 with no unnecessary excipients. USP grade. The reference for D3 supplementation in allergy-sensitive or autoimmune-condition patients.

products.name: Vitamin D3 2000 IU
products.summary: USP verified bulk vitamin D3. Costco import. Excellent cost-per-dose ratio for a USP-certified product. Limited availability in India.

products.name: Fish Oil 1000mg
products.summary: USP verified fish oil, 300mg EPA+DHA per 1g. Costco import. Low cost per serving for a certified product. TOTOX documentation is available on request.

products.name: Omega 3 6 9 Flaxseed
products.summary: Flaxseed-only omega blend. No EPA or DHA. ALA conversion in humans is below 5%. The omega-3 label is technically correct but functionally misleading.

products.name: CoQ10 100mg
products.summary: Ubiquinone at 100mg. Not the superior ubiquinol form. Adequate for young users where conversion efficiency is higher. No COA.

products.name: Alpha Lipoic Acid 600mg
products.summary: ALA at 600mg — the dose used in diabetic neuropathy trials. No COA. Correct dose and form. Carbamide Forte has NABL documentation if that matters.

products.name: NAC 600mg
products.summary: N-acetyl cysteine at 600mg — the dose used in respiratory and antioxidant RCTs. No COA. Correct dose. Carbamide Forte has better documentation.

products.name: Vitamin C 1000mg
products.summary: Ascorbic acid at 1g per tablet. No rose hip or bioflavonoids. Clean single-ingredient vitamin C at the correct dose. No COA published.

products.name: Calcium + D3
products.summary: Calcium citrate with D3 at 400 IU. Calcium form is correct. D3 dose is insufficient to meaningfully support calcium absorption. Half a good idea.

products.name: Iron Bisglycinate 25mg
products.summary: Ferrous bisglycinate at 25mg — the gentle form. No COA but the form selection is correct and the dose is within the therapeutic maintenance range.

products.name: Biotin 10000mcg
products.summary: Biotin at 10mg per tablet. Correct dose for hair and nail RCT evidence. No COA. Form (d-biotin) is correct. Carbamide Forte has NABL documentation.

products.name: Vitamin B12 5000mcg
products.summary: Methylcobalamin at 5000mcg for active deficiency correction. Correct form. High dose is appropriate for correcting existing deficiency — not maintenance.

products.name: Vitamin K2 MK7 200mcg
products.summary: MK-7 at 200mcg — above most commercial doses and closer to the Knapen et al. trial dose (180mcg). Batch COA on Nutrabay website.

products.name: Evening Primrose Oil
products.summary: GLA at approximately 80mg per 1g softgel. Women's hormonal support via GLA pathway. Evidence for PMS and mastalgia is modest but real.

products.name: Activated Charcoal
products.summary: Activated charcoal capsules marketed for bloating and detox. Evidence for GI comfort is anecdotal. Clinical use is limited to poisoning management.

products.name: Probiotics 30 Billion
products.summary: Multi-strain probiotic at 30B CFU. Strain identity disclosed for 5 of 6 strains. Storage stability in Indian logistics is the unverified variable.

products.name: Klean Creatine
products.summary: NSF Certified for Sport. Single-ingredient creatine monohydrate at 5g. Designed for tested athletes — the certification is genuinely meaningful here.

products.name: Creatine
products.summary: NSF Certified for Sport creatine monohydrate. 5g per serving. Thorne's quality standard is among the most rigorous available on import in India.

products.name: Sport Organic Creatine
products.summary: Certified organic, NSF certified creatine monohydrate. 5g per serving. The only organic-certified creatine available in India on import.

products.name: Creatine
products.summary: Pharmaceutical-grade creatine monohydrate. USP grade. Hypoallergenic formulation. The reference for supplementing creatine alongside medical conditions.

products.name: Creatine Monohydrate
products.summary: Nutrabay's mid-tier house label creatine. 5g scoop, batch COA on website. Between the premium and budget Nutrabay tiers on documentation depth.

products.name: Creatine Sour Candy
products.summary: Flavoured creatine at 3g per serving — below the maintenance standard. The flavouring is well-received but the dose is the fundamental problem.

products.name: Creatine Monohydrate
products.summary: Generic creatine at 5g per serving. No COA. Correct dose. The brand's supplement line lacks the analytical credibility of their stronger categories.

products.name: Creatine Surge
products.summary: Creatine with electrolytes and vitamin B. The additions are at irrelevant doses. The 5g creatine is the only thing doing work here.

products.name: Creatine Monohydrate
products.summary: New US brand with Informed Sport interest. Monohydrate at 5g. Clean label. Documentation culture is above the domestic average for the price.

products.name: Creapure Creatine
products.summary: Avvatar's premium creatine line claiming Creapure. If confirmed, this is the best-value domestic Creapure option. COA on request from Avvatar.

products.name: Rhodiola Ashwagandha Stack
products.summary: Rhodiola 400mg with KSM-66 600mg in a single capsule. Both at clinical doses. Batch COA. The most complete anti-fatigue adaptogen stack domestically.

products.name: Ashwagandha Men
products.summary: Ashwagandha with safed musli and shilajit at undisclosed extract specifications. Male health positioning without the ingredient specification to back it.

products.name: Sensoril Plus
products.summary: Sensoril at 250mg with BioPerine 5mg. The piperine addition with Sensoril is unusual — withanolide absorption is well-documented without it.

products.name: Stress Relief Complex
products.summary: Multi-herb stress formula. Ashwagandha, rhodiola, and holy basil at undisclosed doses. No single herb is at a clinical dose in this combination.

products.name: Brahmi Bacopa 500mg
products.summary: Bacopa monnieri at 500mg without bacoside standardisation. Brahmi evidence is real but requires standardised extract to be reliably applied.

products.name: Centella Gotu Kola
products.summary: Centella asiatica at 400mg. Cognitive and wound-healing evidence is modest but real. Standardisation to asiaticoside content is not disclosed.

products.name: Lion's Mane Extract
products.summary: Hericium erinaceus extract at 500mg with beta-glucan percentage disclosed. Growing neurotropic evidence. Better specified than most lion's mane products.

products.name: Schisandra Berry
products.summary: Schisandra chinensis at 500mg. Adaptogenic herb with liver protection and fatigue evidence. No standardisation to schisandrins — the key actives.

products.name: Holy Basil Tulsi
products.summary: Ocimum sanctum extract at 400mg. Anti-stress and mild immunomodulatory evidence. No eugenol standardisation. Correct traditional adaptogen use.

products.name: Fenugreek Extract
products.summary: Fenugreek at 500mg standardised to 50% saponins. Real evidence for blood sugar and modest testosterone effect. Correctly standardised.

products.name: Artichoke Extract
products.summary: Cynara scolymus at 300mg. Modest LDL-lowering and liver-support evidence. Cynarin content not specified — the active compound for cholesterol effects.

products.name: Beet Root Powder
products.summary: Beetroot powder providing dietary nitrates. Performance evidence for endurance is genuine at 500mg nitrate-equivalent doses. Clean food supplement.

products.name: Ashwagandha Shilajit Gold
products.summary: Three-ingredient formula with ashwagandha, shilajit, and gold. Gold is at irrelevant pharmacological doses. No specification for ashwagandha or shilajit.

products.name: Arjuna Terminalia
products.summary: Arjuna bark at 500mg with some tannin standardisation noted. The cardiovascular evidence for arjuna is the strongest in Indian herbal medicine.

products.name: Hawthorn Berry
products.summary: Crataegus extract at 300mg standardised to 2% vitexin. Cardiovascular evidence for hawthorn is moderate for mild hypertension and cardiac function.

products.name: Saffron Extract
products.summary: Saffron at 30mg standardised to 2% safranal — the dose used in depression and mood RCTs. Correct specification. Growing evidence base.

products.name: Saffron Extract 30mg
products.summary: Saffron at 30mg, 2% safranal. NABL COA. The most documented domestic saffron supplement for mood and cognitive support. Correctly specified.

products.name: Lavender Essential Oil
products.summary: Topical lavender oil — not an internal supplement. Oral lavender capsules (Silexan) have some anxiety evidence but this is a topical product.

products.name: Giloy Guduchi Capsule
products.summary: Tinospora cordifolia at 500mg in capsule form. Better than juice format for dose control. No standardisation to immunosides — the active compounds.

products.name: Gudmar Gymnema
products.summary: Gymnema sylvestre at 400mg standardised to 25% gymnemic acids. Appetite and blood glucose evidence is modest. Correct standardisation cited.

products.name: Whey Protein Isolate
products.summary: New domestic brand with isolate claim at honest protein percentage (~89%). Better-specified than average new entrant. COA on request from brand.

products.name: Whey Protein Blend
products.summary: Mid-tier domestic blend. Label transparency is acceptable. NABL COA would close the gap between this and the documented leaders.

products.name: Whey Concentrate 80
products.summary: Online-only brand. 80% protein-per-100g claim is roughly accurate based on published nutrition panel. No COA to independently verify.

products.name: Wheat Germ Oil
products.summary: Wheat germ oil for vitamin E and octacosanol. Modest endurance evidence for octacosanol. The vitamin E content is real but form is not specified.

products.name: Flaxseed Oil
products.summary: ALA-rich flaxseed oil at 1g. ALA conversion to EPA/DHA is below 5%. Useful for omega-6 to omega-3 ratio improvement but not an EPA/DHA substitute.

products.name: Garcinia Cambogia HCA
products.summary: HCA at 60% standardisation. Multiple meta-analyses show small, inconsistent weight effects. The evidence does not support the marketing.

products.name: L-Carnitine 500mg
products.summary: L-carnitine tartrate at 500mg. Correct form. Evidence for fat oxidation in trained athletes is modest. 500mg is below the 2g dose used in most RCTs.

products.name: Ashwagandha Extract 500mg
products.summary: Root extract at 500mg — between the KSM-66 600mg standard and generic powder. No withanolide specification. Plausible but not optimally documented.

products.name: Collagen Type 2
products.summary: Undenatured type II collagen at 40mg — the clinically studied dose for joint immunological tolerance. The correct dose for the correct endpoint.

products.name: Collagen Type 2 Undenatured
products.summary: UC-II at 40mg — the licensed extract used in knee osteoarthritis RCTs. NABL COA. The domestic benchmark for documented type II collagen.

products.name: Methyl Folate 1mg
products.summary: 5-MTHF at 1mg — the bioavailable folate form for MTHFR carriers. Correct form at a higher dose than the 400mcg maintenance level.

products.name: Inositol 1000mg
products.summary: Myo-inositol at 1g. Evidence for PCOS management is strongest at 2-4g/day — this dose is sub-therapeutic for the primary indication.

products.name: Myo-Inositol 2000mg
products.summary: Myo-inositol at 2g — the minimum effective dose for PCOS management in RCTs. NABL COA. Correctly positioned for the evidence base.

products.name: Melatonin 10mg
products.summary: 10mg melatonin — five to ten times the minimum effective dose. Effective but chronically supraphysiological. Higher dose does not mean better sleep.

products.name: Turmeric Milk Mix
products.summary: Turmeric powder with black pepper and milk solids — traditional haldi doodh. Not a standardised curcumin supplement. No curcuminoid quantification.

products.name: Coconut Oil MCT
products.summary: MCT oil from coconut. Caprylic and capric acid at undisclosed percentages. Evidence for ketone production and satiety is modest. Not a fat-loss supplement.

products.name: MCT Oil C8 C10
products.summary: MCT oil with C8 (caprylic acid) and C10 (capric acid) percentage disclosed. NABL COA. Better specified than most MCT products. Evidence for ketosis: moderate.

products.name: Ashwagandha Ginger Turmeric
products.summary: Triple combination at undisclosed doses. No extract specifications for any of the three. Immune and anti-inflammatory marketing without clinical dosing.

products.name: Immunity Booster
products.summary: Vitamin C, zinc, and elderberry at partially disclosed doses. Zinc form is not specified. Elderberry evidence for immunity is limited and modest.

products.name: Elderberry Extract
products.summary: Sambucus nigra extract at 500mg. Immunity and antiviral evidence is modest — most compelling data is from influenza studies. Correct use case.

products.name: Echinacea Extract
products.summary: Echinacea purpurea at 400mg. Cold duration reduction evidence is modest and inconsistent across meta-analyses. Correct herb, uncertain benefit.

products.name: Licorice Root DGL
products.summary: Deglycyrrhizinated licorice (DGL) at 500mg. DGL removes glycyrrhizin — the BP-raising compound. GI ulcer and acid reflux evidence is real.

products.name: Ashwagandha Testomax
products.summary: Ashwagandha at undisclosed specification with tribulus and fenugreek. The testosterone support claim requires documented extract specifications — absent here.

products.name: Liver Protect
products.summary: Milk thistle, dandelion, and artichoke combination. Milk thistle is the only component with strong liver evidence. Others are at decorative doses.

products.name: Probiotic 60 Billion
products.summary: Multi-strain probiotic at 60B CFU. Strain identity is partially disclosed. High CFU count is a marketing point — strain identity matters more than CFU.

products.name: Digestive Probiotics
products.summary: Probiotic blend with 5 strains at 10B CFU. Strain identity disclosed. Adequate entry-level probiotic. Stability in Indian supply chain is the unknown.

products.name: Hair Skin Nails
products.summary: Multi-nutrient formula for hair, skin, and nails. Biotin at 5000mcg (correct dose). Other ingredients at sub-clinical amounts. Biotin is carrying the formula.

products.name: NMN 250mg
products.summary: NMN at 250mg — in the range used in early human trials. Longevity supplement. Evidence tier: early-stage human RCT, promising but not settled.

products.name: Trans Resveratrol 250mg
products.summary: Trans-resveratrol at 250mg — the bioavailable isomer. Correct form. Longevity evidence remains preliminary. Better specified than most Indian resveratrol.

products.name: PQQ 20mg
products.summary: Pyrroloquinoline quinone at 20mg. Mitochondrial biogenesis evidence is early-stage. Human trial evidence is limited. Niche longevity supplement.

products.name: PQQ + CoQ10
products.summary: PQQ at 20mg with CoQ10 at 100mg ubiquinone. NABL COA. The combination targets mitochondrial function from two directions. Correctly specified.

products.name: Spermidine
products.summary: Spermidine from wheat germ at 1mg — the dose used in early longevity trials. Very early human evidence. Correctly cautious but the dose is minimal.

products.name: Urolithin A
products.summary: Urolithin A at 250mg — the mitophagy-activating compound from pomegranate metabolism. Early human trial evidence. Mitopure is the benchmark extract.

products.name: Urolithin A 500mg
products.summary: Urolithin A at 500mg. NABL COA. Better dose than most domestic options. Evidence is early-stage but growing — muscle and longevity RCTs underway.
